Method 2 transforms 2D projection images into 2D spectral matrices via Fourier transform, combines all 2D matrices into a 3D matrix, extracts a 2D matrix indicating 3D characteristics by analyzing the functional expression of the optical field distribution, and encodes the 2D matrix to obtain the hologram [S4].

where $C_2, C_3$ are known parameters of the color/alpha map at endpoints with voxel values $I_2, I_3$ [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that C2 and C3 are known parameters of the color/alpha map at endpoints with voxel values I2 and I3. Source [S3] explicitly provides Equation (1): Cx = C3 - (C3 - C2)(I3 - Ix) / (I3 - I2). The text immediately following this equation states: 'where C2, C3, I2, and I3 are the known parameters of the color map and α map. Ix is the value of voxel x.' Although the text does not explicitly repeat 'at endpoints' in the definition sentence, the structure of the linear interpolation formula (using I2 and I3 as the denominator bounds for Ix) and the context of 'color map and alpha map' (which typically define values at specific endpoints or control points) confirms that I2 and I3 correspond to the endpoints associated with parameters C2 and C3. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
supported

For each voxel $x$ with value $I_x$, calculate its color components $C_x$ (where $C \in \{R, G, B, \alpha\}$) using linear interpolation on the provided maps [S3, unofficial]:

The claim states that for each voxel $x$ with value $I_x$, the color components $C_x$ are calculated using linear interpolation on provided maps. The evidence in Source [S3] explicitly confirms this in Section 3.1, stating: 'First, initialize the color and opacity information based on the color map, α map, and each voxel value... Cx is calculated with Eq. (1). Cx=C3−(C3−C2)(I3−Ix)/(I3−I2), where C2, C3, I2, and I3 are the known parameters of the color map and α map. Ix is the value of voxel x.' This equation represents linear interpolation between two endpoints (I2, C2) and (I3, C3) to find the value Cx for an intermediate voxel value Ix. The claim accurately reflects the method described in the evidence.

For a voxel $eli$, calculate the incident light intensity $I_{di}$ from the light source [S3, unofficial].

This matches the claim that the incident light intensity is calculated from the light source.
